parsed_artifact.argument_markdown:
## Setup and conventions

Work over a field of characteristic 0. Let B be locally of finite type, and let π:C→B be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected genus-6 curves equipped with a balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl structure: a finite flat degree-4 morphism γ:C→P:=P^1_B, a rank-3 vector bundle E on P, and a splitting of the CE relations bundle F≅O_P(4)⊕O_P(5). Following the packet CE convention (and the degree-compatible reading of SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6), define

W_f := (O_{P(E^∨)}(2) ⊗ γ^* O_P(−f))|_C, f∈{4,5}.

Thus W_5 is the f_2=5 summand of (O(2)⊗γ^*F^∨)|_C and is not the O_P(5) summand of F. Write W:=W_4⊕W_5 and L:=W_5⊗ω_{C/B}^{−1}. The packet sign γ^*O(−f) is mandatory: the opposite sign would reverse the contribution of γ to deg(W_f) and destroy the degree-zero balance of the f=5 obstruction at n=6.

Let Conf_6(C/B) be the open substack of C^6_B of ordered 6-tuples of pairwise distinct sections, with universal ordered divisor Γ=p_1+⋯+p_6. Define

- Z_ev ⊂ Conf_6(C/B): geometric points with H^0(C_b, ω_{C_b}⊗W^∨(Γ_b))≠0 (CE residual evaluation-failure);
- I ⊂ Conf_6(C/B): geometric points with O_{C_b}(Γ_b)≅L_b (Abel–Jacobi incidence for L).

Both are closed in Conf_6(C/B) as zero loci of coherent obstruction sheaves (resp. as the fibre product of the Abel–Jacobi map against the section classifying L).

## Step 1 (source-backed): degree of W_f

By SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 under the convention W_f=(O_{P(E^∨)}(2)⊗γ^*O(−f))|_C,

deg(W_f|_C) = 2(2g−2+4·2) − 4f = 4g+12−4f.

At g=6 this gives deg(W_5)=4·6+12−4·5=16 and deg(W_4)=4·6+12−4·4=20. Since deg(ω_C)=2g−2=10,

deg(L)=deg(W_5)−deg(ω_C)=16−10=6.

(Internal consistency: deg(O_{P(E^∨)}(1)|_C)=2g−2+8=18 and γ has degree 4, so 2·18−4f=36−4f=4g+12−4f.)

## Step 2 (proved): obstruction degrees at (g,n)=(6,6)

SRC-0004 supplies deg(ω_C⊗W_f^∨(Γ))=2g−2−(4g+12−4f)+n=4f+n−2g−14 for any effective divisor Γ of degree n. Substituting g=6, n=6:

- f=4: 16+6−12−14=−4;
- f=5: 20+6−12−14=0.

Equivalently deg(ω_C)−deg(W_f)+n equals 10−20+6=−4 and 10−16+6=0.

## Step 3 (proved): vanishing of the f=4 summand

On a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, a line bundle of negative degree has no nonzero global section (a nonzero section would cut an effective divisor of nonnegative degree). Hence for every effective degree-six Γ,

H^0(C, ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=0.

## Step 4 (proved): degree-zero criterion for the f=5 summand

On a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, a degree-zero line bundle N admits a nonzero global section if and only if N≅O_C: a nonzero section has effective vanishing divisor of degree 0, hence is nowhere vanishing, so O_C→N is an isomorphism. Applying this to N=ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ) of degree 0 yields

H^0(C, ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))≠0 ⇔ ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ)≅O_C ⇔ O_C(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω_C^{−1}=L.

(This uses only effectivity of vanishing divisors, not Serre duality.)

## Step 5 (proved on geometric fibres): residual evaluation fails iff Abel–Jacobi incidence

On geometric fibres the balanced splitting F≅O(4)⊕O(5) induces W≅W_4⊕W_5, and SRC-0004 splits the residual obstruction:

H^0(C, ω_C⊗W^∨(Γ)) = H^0(ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ)) ⊕ H^0(ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ)).

Steps 3–4 therefore give H^0(ω_C⊗W^∨(Γ))≠0 if and only if O_C(Γ)≅L. Consequently Z_ev and I have the same geometric points over every geometric fibre of B, and

(Z_ev)_red = I_red

as reduced closed substacks of Conf_6(C/B). This is the packet six-point failure condition derived from the f_2=5 summand with the sign γ^*O(−5).

## Step 6 (proved): Riemann–Roch nonemptiness of the full residual system

On every smooth genus-6 geometric fibre, χ(L)=deg(L)−g+1=6−6+1=1, so h^0(L)=1+h^1(L)≥1. Thus the relative Abel–Jacobi fibre of L in Sym^6_{C/B} is fibrewise nonempty: every geometric fibre carries at least one (possibly non-reduced) effective degree-six divisor linearly equivalent to L. Equivalently, the unordered residual incidence in Sym^6 is nonempty. (This matches the packet finding FND-0005 at the level of the full linear system; it does not by itself produce a reduced six-point configuration on every fibre.)

## Step 7 (proved on stacks): ordered reduced model as finite étale S_6-torsor

Inside the relative effective-divisor space of degree six, the locus of reduced-support divisors (six pairwise-distinct geometric points) is open: it is the complement of the image of the big diagonal under a finite (hence closed) map. It is not closed, because fibrewise Sym^6 is irreducible and contains non-reduced divisors (e.g. 6p). Over that reduced-support open, the natural map from the stack of ordered pairwise-distinct 6-tuples is a finite étale S_6-torsor: S_6 acts freely by permuting labels, and free actions of finite groups yield étale torsors. Restricting to I_red yields a finite étale S_6-torsor

I_red → I^{red-supp}

onto the reduced-support open of the relative Abel–Jacobi fibre of L. This is the packet model: ordered distinct reduced divisors as a finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open; that open is not called closed. Freeness can fail on coarse moduli at curves with automorphisms permuting marked points, so the torsor statement is at stack level.

## Identification of Z (C66-GEO-Z)

The evaluation-failure locus Z of the balanced tetragonal CE geometry, in the ordered reduced model over a balanced CE base, is the reduced closed substack I_red=(Z_ev)_red ⊂ Conf_6(C/B) cut out by O_C(Γ)≅L=W_5⊗ω^{−1}. Its unordered reduced model is the reduced-support open I^{red-supp} of the residual linear system of L, with finite étale S_6 ordering cover. This completes the construction and reduced identification required by C66-GEO-Z.

## Explicit non-claims (downstream or open)

1. Scheme-theoretic (non-reduced) equality of the CE determinantal/Fitting rank-drop ideal of Z_ev with the Abel–Jacobi ideal of I is not claimed: geometric-point agreement determines only reduced structures (C66-COMP-RANK / Fitting comparison).
2. Fibrewise nonemptiness of I^{red-supp} (or of ordered reduced Z_ev) on every geometric fibre is not claimed: χ(L)=1 only forces the full Sym^6 fibre to be nonempty; reduced members require base-point-freeness of L and a Bertini argument (or an equivalent special-fibre analysis).
3. The residual duality identification W_5≅ω_C^{⊗2}(−D) for a fibre class D of γ is not used and not claimed; the failure condition is stated intrinsically in terms of W_5.
4. Global well-definedness of the direct-sum splitting W=W_4⊕W_5 and of L over bases where F does not split, or up to Pic(B) twists of relative O_P(−f), is restricted to geometric fibres / actual balanced splittings as in the setup.
5. h^0-stratification of |L|, components, dimensions, stabilizers, maps to tetragonal moduli or to M_{6,6}, and any Gysin/Tate statement for W_{−16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) are outside C66-GEO-Z (C66-GEO-H0, C66-GEO-COMP, C66-TATE-*).

## Blocked routes (not used)

- vcd-only-vanishing: unused; no cohomological vanishing argument appears.
- undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex: unused; no graph-complex input.
- point-count-without-degree-parity-separation: unused; no point-counting.
- forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown: unused; no forgetful-map or local-system renaming.

## Relation to the exact target

The ambient exact theorem asserts that W_{−16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q)≅W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) is a direct sum of Q(8). The present lemma only constructs and identifies the geometric locus Z on which later support and assembly arguments act. It does not resolve RED-0001.

parsed_artifact.theorem_statement: Let B be a locally finite-type scheme over a field of characteristic 0, and let π:C→B be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected curves of genus 6 equipped with a balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl structure: a finite flat degree-4 morphism γ:C→P:=P^1_B together with a splitting F≅O_P(4)⊕O_P(5) of the CE relations bundle and the associated rank-3 bundle E on P. For f∈{4,5} put W_f:=(O_{P(E^∨)}(2)⊗γ^*O_P(−f))|_C (so W_5 is the f_2=5 summand of (O(2)⊗γ^*F^∨)|_C, not the O_P(5) summand of F), write W:=W_4⊕W_5, and put L:=W_5⊗ω_{C/B}^{−1}. Let Conf_6(C/B) be the open substack of the relative 6-fold fibre product C×_B⋯×_B C parametrizing ordered 6-tuples of pairwise distinct sections, with universal ordered divisor Γ=p_1+⋯+p_6. Define Z_ev⊂Conf_6(C/B) as the closed locus of geometric points at which H^0(C_b,ω_{C_b}⊗W^∨(Γ_b))≠0 (CE residual evaluation-failure), and I⊂Conf_6(C/B) as the closed locus of geometric points at which O_{C_b}(Γ_b)≅L_b (Abel–Jacobi incidence for L). Then for every geometric fibre C and every ordered pairwise-distinct effective degree-six divisor Γ on C: (i) deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12−4f, so deg(W_5)=16, deg(W_4)=20, and deg(L)=6; (ii) deg(ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=−4 and deg(ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))=0; (iii) H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=0; (iv) H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))≠0 if and only if O_C(Γ)≅L; (v) therefore H^0(C,ω_C⊗W^∨(Γ))≠0 if and only if O_C(Γ)≅L, so Z_ev and I have the same geometric points and (Z_ev)_red=I_red as reduced closed substacks of Conf_6(C/B); (vi) if I^{red-supp} denotes the open locus of reduced-support effective divisors in the relative Abel–Jacobi fibre of L over B, then the natural ordering map I_red→I^{red-supp} is a finite étale S_6-torsor of algebraic stacks (on the stack of pairwise-distinct sections). In particular the packet six-point failure condition O_C(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω_C^{−1} is exactly the geometric residual CE evaluation-failure locus under the γ^*O(−5) convention, and the ordered reduced model of Z is the finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open in that residual linear system. This identifies Z at the reduced/set-theoretic level required by C66-GEO-Z; it does not assert scheme-theoretic equality of Fitting/determinantal ideals with the Abel–Jacobi ideal, fibrewise reduced-support nonemptiness on every geometric fibre, an h^0-stratification, component dimensions or stabilizers, a closed pure-codimension embedding into M_{6,6}, or any Tate-type claim about W_{−16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q).
